events.region: Laurens; Central Greenville; Southern Greenville; Northern Spartanburg; Southern Spartanburg
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
At 946 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms with torrential
rainfall along a line extending from 11 miles west of Spartanburg to
11 miles south of Greenville Downtown, and moving southeast at 20
mph.

Locations to be impacted include...
Laurens, Spartanburg, Greenville Eastside, Greer, Mauldin,
Simpsonville, Five Forks, Fountain Inn, Woodruff, and Duncan.

Very heavy rainfall rates up to 2 inches per hour will be possible in
these areas.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is ongoing.

* WHERE...A portion of eastern North Carolina, including the
following county, Dare.

* WHEN...Until 245 PM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water over roadways.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 933 AM EDT, local law enforcement reported that portions
of NC12 remain underwater this morning with Dare County
Communications center reporting 4-5" across the roadway near
Pea Island. Overflowing poor drainage areas have already
caused minor flooding in the advisory area.
- Flooding impacts will continue, but no additional rainfall is
expected.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
the vicinity of Pea Island National Wildlife Refuge
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

decline late this afternoon through the end of the week.

* IMPACTS...Moderate. Strong breaking waves and strong currents
will make swimming dangerous.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Three Rivers affecting Live Oak County.

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County.

Nueces River At Cotulla affecting La Salle County.

For the Nueces River...including Cotulla, Tilden, Three Rivers,
Mathis, Bluntzer, Calallen...Major flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Three Rivers.

* WHEN...From Tuesday evening until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 40.0 feet, Significant flooding reaches miles from the
main channel, flooding homes in the flood plain near Three Rivers
to Lake Corpus Christi. Up to 4 feet of water is in River Creek
Acres Subdivision, flooding several homes. Kellner Camp along
County Road 336 floods, with water several feet deep surrounding
homes. Antelope Lane is flooded cutting off access to J.I. Hailey
Subdivision at Jones River bend. Water approaches the base of homes
along the river in Buckeye Knoll Subdivision, 2 miles west of
Swinny Switch.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:15 AM CDT Sunday the stage was 3.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 20.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late
Tuesday evening and continue rising to 40.4 feet Friday morning.
Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 25.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 40.6
feet on 07/11/2007.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.summary:

Nueces River Near Three Rivers affecting Live Oak County.

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County.

Nueces River At Cotulla affecting La Salle County.

For the Nueces River...including Cotulla, Tilden, Three Rivers,
Mathis, Bluntzer, Calallen...Major flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Tilden.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 20.0 feet, Major flooding below Cotulla to below
Tilden occurs, and cuts off extensive portions of the flood plain,
requiring wholesale evacuation of livestock from the area. Roads
and bridges near the river flood severely. Hunting cabins, pump
jacks, tank batteries, irrigation pumps and any equipment in low
areas near the river flood.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 AM CDT Sunday the stage was 10.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 11.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late
this morning and continue rising to a crest of 23.1 feet tomorrow
evening.
- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 23.1
feet on 09/18/2002.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.region: Keokuk; Washington; Louisa; Jefferson; Henry; Des Moines; Van Buren; Lee; Henry; Mercer; Henderson; Warren; Hancock; McDonough; Scotland; Clark
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
Light winds and very humid conditions have resulted in areas of
fog this morning, some dense, mainly south of I-80 in southeast
Iowa, west central Illinois, and northeast Missouri. In places
this fog is reducing visibility to near one quarter mile. Expect
conditions to gradually improve between 900 AM and 1030 AM as the
fog dissipates.

Motorists should exercise caution as visibilities may change
suddenly over short distances. Use low beam headlights and leave
plenty of distance between you and the vehicle ahead.
